source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Store medicines and cleaners within reach if containers have child-resistant caps, because extra safeguards add little.","B":"Rely on supervision alone, because furniture anchoring and electrical or fire-safety devices are usually unnecessary.","C":"Delay home safety changes until school age, because younger children naturally avoid most household hazards.","D":"Use age-appropriate safeguards such as locked medicines, anchored furniture, smoke alarms, and protected outlets."}}
source_row.rationale: Young-child injury prevention uses layered environmental controls such as anchoring furniture, securing toxic products and medicines, maintaining smoke alarms and using age-appropriate barriers and outlet protection.
source_row.source_detail: CPSC childproofing recommendations address furniture/TV anchoring, locked storage of medicines and household chemicals, smoke alarms and age-appropriate home safety devices. Current U.S. CPSC childproofing safety guide rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.source_name: U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission — Childproofing Your Home
source_row.stem: Which household intervention is appropriate for preventing common injuries in young children?
